subject: Failed Convergence: Latent Variables in CLPM

messages.author: 5ce1f1f0b0b32cf2
messages.subject: Failed Convergence: Latent Variables in CLPM
parts:
Dear Group,

I have tried creating latent variables to add in to my cross-lagged panel model using the following code: 

Note: CHRONO and getup are 4-level ordinal variables.

cl_ld_2 <-
  '

# LVs
phase_0 =~ CHRONO_0 + getup_0
phase_1 =~ CHRONO_1 + getup_1

#Regressions
phase_1 ~ phase_0 + LOG_avLight
LOG_avLight_1 ~ phase_0 + LOG_avLight


#Covariances
phase_0 ~~ LOG_avLight
phase_1 ~~ LOG_avLight_1
'
fit_cl_ld_2 <- sem(cl_ld_2, data=d1, ordered=c('CHRONO_0', 'CHRONO_1', 'GET_UP_0','GET_UP_1'), estimator='PML',std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

summary(fit_cl_ld_2, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T)

For some reason this fails to converge with the following message: 

"convergence status (0=ok):  0
nlminb message says:  relative convergence (4)
number of iterations:  1409
number of function evaluations [objective, gradient]:  1861 1410
Fitting baseline model ...  done.
Warning message:
In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged,
                  but not all elements of the gradient are (near) zero;
                  the optimizer may not have found a local solution
                  use check.gradient = FALSE to skip this check."

Any idea why this might be the case? I have successfully done this with a very similar model that also uses ordinal variables to indicate the latent variables. 

So I have arrived at the conclusion that it has something to do with the two variables I am using to indicate with but I can't figure out what. 

The CHRONO and getup variables are not redundant (correlated at .47) so I wouldn't think it would be that? 

I would really appreciate some help with this and thanks in advance for any advice. 

Kind regards,

Angus

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Failed Convergence: Latent Variables in CLPM
parts:
It is likely that your model is underidentified, especially with only
two indicators per factor, and those categorical. In particular,
phase_1 is probably not identified. Try constraining the two phase
variables to measurement invariance (loadings and thresholds).
std.lv=TRUE is also probably not what you want for longitudinal data.

Pat

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Failed Convergence: Latent Variables in CLPM
parts:
Measurement invariance for categorical indicators is most commonly
defined as loading and threshold invariance simultaneously.

So loadings looks something like this:

phase_0 =~ 1*CHRONO_0 + l1*getup_0
phase_1 =~ 1*CHRONO_1 + l1*getup_1

That still may not identify it, depending on other details--there
might need to be some additional constraints on l1.

I don't have a lot of experience with manipulating thresholds in
lavaan, but they use a | syntax for each ordinal variable. Online
tutorials or someone else here should be able to help with that
syntax.

Pat

I tried this but apparently the syntax "|1*getup_0" is incorrect for defining thresholds and I can't seem to find a tutorial online anyplace. Could you recommend one?

Furthermore, this is quite strange as I have another model that runs perfectly fine and is also using 4-level ordinal indicators for LVs... So it is odd that this would be any different. 

Is it feasible/possible to constrain the variance of an LV to be positive?

Perplexed!

Regards,

Angus

On Wednesday, July 22, 2020 at 11:43:57 PM UTC+10 mal...@malonequantitative.com wrote:
Measurement invariance for categorical indicators is most commonly
defined as loading and threshold invariance simultaneously.

So loadings looks something like this:

phase_0 =~ 1*CHRONO_0 + l1*getup_0
phase_1 =~ 1*CHRONO_1 + l1*getup_1

That still may not identify it, depending on other details--there
might need to be some additional constraints on l1.

I don't have a lot of experience with manipulating thresholds in
lavaan, but they use a | syntax for each ordinal variable. Online
tutorials or someone else here should be able to help with that
syntax.

Pat

messages.subject: Re: Failed Convergence: Latent Variables in CLPM
parts: apparently the syntax "|1*getup_0" is incorrect

The correct syntax is with the variable name on the lefthand side, and the thresholds are sequenced t1, t2, etc.

getup_0 | thresholdLabel*t1  

Look into the semTools::measEq.syntax() function (and help-page examples) to help you write invariance models with categorical indicators.  But it is only for CFA models, so you would test invariance in the context of the CFA first, then upon establishing invariance, you could add a latent structural model.
